title: 10-Year Yield Back Above 5% as Treasuries Reopen and a December Hike Stays Priced In
dek: Treasury trading resumed after Veterans Day with the 10-year yield above 5%, jobless claims rose to 200,000, and CME FedWatch still shows a quarter-point December hike as the base case.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Black-and-white photograph of an automatic ticker apparatus on the New York Stock Exchange trading floor
image.credit: Library of Congress via Wikimedia Commons

keyPoints: The 10-year Treasury yield rose more than 7 basis points to 5.068% when bond trading resumed Thursday (CNBC).
The 2-year note rose more than 11 basis points to 4.843%, and the 30-year bond rose more than 5 basis points to 5.40% (CNBC).
Initial jobless claims rose 9,000 to 200,000 in the week ended Nov. 7, the Labor Department said at 8:30 a.m. ET (DOL release, via Anadolu Agency).
CME FedWatch prices a 100% chance of a quarter-point December hike, with about 13% odds of a half-point move (CNBC).
body:
The US bond market reopened Thursday after the Veterans Day holiday, and yields moved sharply higher. The 10-year Treasury yield, the benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit cards, rose more than 7 basis points to 5.068%, CNBC reported. That puts it back above 5% after Tuesday's hotter-than-expected consumer price report.

## The curve

The move was broad. The 2-year note, which is most sensitive to near-term Fed policy, rose more than 11 basis points to 4.843%. The 30-year bond rose more than 5 basis points to 5.40% (CNBC). A sharper rise at the front end than at the long end points to a market repricing Fed policy rather than only long-run inflation fears.

Oil was part of the story. West Texas Intermediate gained 0.4% to $86.86 a barrel and Brent was about 1% higher at $93.60, after President Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran (CNBC). Higher energy prices feed inflation expectations, which pushes yields up.

## Jobless claims

The Labor Department said initial jobless claims rose by 9,000 to a seasonally adjusted 200,000 in the week ended Nov. 7, above economists' forecasts (DOL release, via Anadolu Agency). The figure does not point to a labor market under strain, and it did not give the Fed a reason to ease its hike bets.

## The December decision

Traders still price a quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 FOMC meeting as the base case. CME FedWatch shows about 13% odds of a half-point move, CNBC reported. FedRateCalc and Tickward list the meeting for Dec. 8-9, with the decision due Dec. 9 at 2 p.m. ET.

The next inflation test is Friday's October producer price index, due at 8:30 a.m. ET on Nov. 13. CNBC said economists expect a 0.4% monthly rise, after a 1.3% jump in September.

This is market analysis, not investment advice. Yield levels are from the cited intraday reports and may have moved since they were published.

marketImpact.summary: Higher yields and a fully priced December hike are the main pressure on rate-sensitive assets. The Friday PPI report is the next data point that could change the hike-size debate.
marketImpact.timeframe: Thursday, Nov. 12, then Friday, Nov. 13 PPI at 8:30 a.m. ET

tickers.rationale: Long-dated Treasury prices fall as yields rise; the 30-year yield rose to 5.40% on the reopening (CNBC)
Bitcoin ETFs have been losing money as higher rates make non-yielding assets harder to hold (Bitcoin Magazine)
